check_description:
This check verifies that `target_assessment.pptx` derives Aurora's fair-value EV/EBITDA range using Halberd's 4-step sequential haircut method anchored on Cal-Maine, with each step shown numerically, and lands its central fair-value EV/EBITDA estimate for Aurora entirely inside the Halberd-mandated FY24 EBITDA range.

The deck must verify all of: (a) Scale haircut applied to Cal-Maine mid-cycle multiple, not raw broker multiples. (b) Private-company discount applied. (c) Risk-specific colony-deadline haircut applied, tied to Aurora's colony exposure. (d) Full calculation chain shown explicitly (not just the final result). (e) The 4 haircut steps display explicit numeric values in a table, decomposition, or sequential block; narrative-only acknowledgement fails. (f) If the central fair-value is given as a point estimate, it must fall within the mandated range. If the central fair-value is given as a range, the entire range must fall within the mandated range. Showing the standards worked-example output and the broker-asking-side framing as supplementary context is acceptable provided the deck explicitly anchors the central case in the mandated range. Anchoring the central case at the worked-example output, at the broker-asking-side framing, at the broker asking directly, or at any range with any portion outside the mandated range fails.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) the deck uses Cal-Maine multiples directly without scale haircut; or (b) no private-company discount; or (c) no risk-specific colony-deadline haircut; or (d) the deck only states the result (e.g., 'fair-value 5-6x') without showing the calculation chain; or (e) haircut chain described narratively without per-step numeric decomposition; or fewer than four numeric haircut steps shown; or haircuts shown only as a final fair-value range without the per-step decomposition; or (f) the central fair-value estimate has any portion outside 5.0-6.5x. A point estimate <5.0x or >6.5x fails. A range with any portion outside 5.0-6.5x fails (e.g., 4.5-6.0x, 4.8-6.3x, 5.5-7.5x, 4.0-8.0x all fail). Common failure modes for (f): anchored at the standards 1.1 worked-example output (4.1-4.6x) without recognising that example uses illustrative inputs; anchored at 8-10x (broker-asking-side framing) without recognising that's a negotiation talking point not the analytical target; anchored at the broker asking 12-14x directly; carries a range whose endpoints fall outside 5.0-6.5x.
score_1_criteria: All of: (a) scale haircut 30-50% applied to the public comp anchor (Cal-Maine ~9-11x mid-cycle or equivalent); (b) private discount 18-28% applied; (c) risk-specific colony-deadline haircut applied (either as additional 1.0-1.5x EBITDA absolute reduction or as an equivalent multiple haircut sized to colony exposure); (d) calculation chain shown (starting multiple -> each haircut -> fair-value range), or an explicit comp valuation chain narrative is included with each haircut named; (e) each of the four haircut steps (cohort multiple -> scale haircut -> private discount -> risk-specific haircut) shows an explicit numeric value in a table, decomposition, or sequential calculation block. The Slack U005 working chain [2026-05-08 ts 1778250000] establishes the chain output verbatim ('Cal-Maine cohort median ~10-11x -> scale haircut ~35-45% -> private discount ~20-25% -> colony-risk haircut tied to Aurora's 40% colony exposure. Lands ~5.0-6.5x FY24 EBITDA'); Vivian's same-day acknowledgement [2026-05-08 ts 1778250120] confirms 5.0-6.5x as the central case. (f) the deck's central fair-value EV/EBITDA estimate for Aurora falls entirely within 5.0-6.5x FY24 EBITDA inclusive (Slack U002 [2026-05-08 ts 1778250120]: '5.0-6.5x as the central case, broker 12-14x lives on the page as the negotiation gap not the central number'; reinforced by Slack U002 [2026-05-08 ts 1778262480]: 'Anchor: 5.0-6.5x'). A point estimate must satisfy 5.0x <= estimate <= 6.5x. A range must satisfy 5.0x <= lower endpoint and upper endpoint <= 6.5x; the endpoints 5.0x and 6.5x are themselves acceptable. A deck that shows both the standards 1.1 worked-example output (4.1-4.6x) and the broker-asking-side haircut (8-10x) as context but explicitly anchors the central / defendable fair-value entirely within 5.0-6.5x passes.

This check verifies that `target_assessment.pptx` surfaces at least three sized bottom-line (cost-out / operational) value-creation levers, each with the full Halberd-mandated economics package.

The deck must verify all of: (a) >=3 named bottom-line levers from the standards categories. Top-line opportunities relabelled as bottom-line fail. (b) Each lever carries an EBITDA uplift figure. (c) Each lever carries a capex / cost-of-implementation figure. (d) Each lever has a payback period named. (e) >=2 levers reference Calthorpe-anchored opportunities within tolerance of source dollar figures.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.

check_description:
This check verifies that `target_assessment.pptx` surfaces the 2027 colony-cage retailer deadline as the #1 risk in a Halberd-mandated risk register, with Aurora's exposure quantified, EBITDA-at-risk sized per the firm's risk-register format, top 3-5 prioritised risks (each $-EBITDA-sized), feed-grain pass-through risk explicitly named, and all three structurally concentrated supply chains identified (day-old chick / breeder genetics; automation / conversion-equipment vendor concentration; packaging single-supplier).

The deck must verify all of: (a) 2027 colony-cage deadline appears as #1 risk (not buried below other risks). (b) Aurora's colony exposure quantified. (c) EBITDA-at-risk per year of slippage sized within tolerance of the source anchor. (d) Probability tag with rationale present. (e) Named mitigant present. (f) Risk register has top 3-5 prioritised risks with $-EBITDA impact per risk; not unprioritised list, not narrative without sizing. (g) Feed-grain pass-through named with quantitative anchor. (h) All three structurally concentrated supply chains named: (h-i) day-old chick / breeder genetics concentration (e.g., EW Group 75-80% global commercial layer genetics); (h-ii) automation / conversion-equipment vendor concentration (Big Dutchman / Vencomatic / Salmet); (h-iii) packaging single-supplier (Huhtamaki Otahuhu moulded-fibre). Conditional vacuity carve-out: if the deck's scope legitimately does not surface one of (h-i)/(h-ii)/(h-iii) because the deck is explicitly scoped to a sub-section that excludes it (e.g., a deck framed only on grow-out / grading rather than on the full upstream stack), the corresponding sub-check passes by vacuity for that chain only; broader supply-chain scope cannot trigger the carve-out.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) colony deadline buried below other risks or omitted; or (b) exposure not quantified; or (c) EBITDA-at-risk not sized or wrong magnitude; or (d) probability tag missing; or (e) mitigant missing; or (f) risk register has more than 5 risks unprioritised or fewer than 3 or no $-EBITDA sizing; or (g) feed-grain pass-through risk absent / present without quantitative anchor; or (h) any of the three structurally concentrated supply chains is unnamed without the vacuity carve-out genuinely applying: (h-i) day-old chick / breeder genetics concentration absent and the deck's scope does engage with upstream supply / input concentration; or (h-ii) automation / conversion-equipment vendor concentration absent and the deck's scope does engage with conversion capex or vendor selection; or (h-iii) packaging single-supplier (Huhtamaki Otahuhu) absent and the deck's scope does engage with downstream packaging / grading operations.

(f) risk register has top 3-5 prioritised risks with $-EBITDA impact per risk (NZ$ figure or equivalent quantification, per IC pre-read § 4 cap); (g) feed-grain pass-through named as a specific risk with quantitative anchor (Calthorpe Part 7 [00:07:18]: 'Feed cost per dozen at FY24 prices is approximately NZ$1.85-2.10 per dozen on the layer flock - that's 55-65% of variable cost' / pass-through lag 4-6 months / Mainland MainFeeds captive vs Aurora commercial-purchasing asymmetry); (h) all three structurally concentrated supply chains named: (h-i) day-old chick / breeder genetics 75-80% EW Group; (h-ii) automation / conversion-equipment Big Dutchman / Vencomatic / Salmet; (h-iii) packaging Huhtamaki Otahuhu single-supplier. check_description:
This check verifies that `target_assessment.pptx` complies with three firm-wide Halberd conventions (the no-recommendation rule, the USD reporting-currency convention, and US English spelling) and ends with the IC-mandated synthesis structure: a key-findings synthesis (sentiment / direction parseable) and a separate prioritised risk register.

The deck must verify all of: (a) No explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing (one-sided promotion implicitly recommends invest). (b) Every dollar figure on the deck is presented in USD. NZD (or other local-currency) figures are permitted ONLY when paired with their USD equivalent on the same slide, and the USD conversion must use the rate from the FX_Rates_Forecast or FX_Rates_Historical tab of halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx that matches the time period of the underlying figure (historical figures use the FY-aligned historical rate for the year of the figure; multi-year forward / DCF figures use the FY-aligned forecast rate per year). A single flat spot rate applied across multi-year forecasts is disallowed. Unsourced spot rates or training-data rates are disallowed. The applied rate(s) and source workbook must be documented (footnote, slide footer, or speaker note). For deliverables with no financial figures (b) is satisfied by default. (c) Distinct key-findings synthesis section with findings within the cap. (d) Findings carry a sentiment / direction signal so positive and negative findings are both surfaced. (e) Separate prioritised risk register with risks within the cap. (f) US English spelling throughout the deliverable (every slide title, body text, footnote, speaker note, chart label, table caption). Halberd is a US private-equity firm; US English is the implicit firm-wide convention. Any single instance of British / Commonwealth spelling fails this sub-criterion - e.g., 'realise' instead of 'realize', 'organise', 'colour', 'centre', 'programme', 'analyse', 'favour', 'behaviour', 'specialise'. Proper-noun spellings retain their canonical form (e.g., 'World Organisation for Animal Health' / WOAH, registered company names, official department names) and do not count as fails.

All sub-criteria must pass; the synthesis section absent entirely is an automatic fail.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation present; or thesis-pillar framing present ('compelling opportunity', 'attractive asset', 'strong fit for the platform'); or (b) any one of: any NZD (or other local-currency) figure appears on the deck without its USD equivalent on the same slide; or USD figures are presented without documentation of the FX rate(s) and source workbook (no footnote / footer / speaker note naming halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx or the FY-aligned rate); or an unsourced spot rate / training-data rate / external-source rate is applied where the central workbook rate was required; or a single flat spot rate is applied across a multi-year forecast (e.g., one USD/NZD rate used for FY2026 through FY2030 figures); or the rate applied does not match the time period of the underlying figure (e.g., an FY2025 historical figure converted at an FY2028 forecast rate, or a forward-year forecast figure converted at an historical rate); or (c) fewer than 3 or more than 5 findings in the synthesis section; or (d) findings are presented as a flat list with no sentiment / direction signal; or (e) no separate prioritised risk register (risks only embedded in narrative without a 3-5 prioritised register); or (f) any single instance of British or Commonwealth spelling in the deck's own prose (excluding proper nouns / registered org names) - e.g., realise, organise, colour, centre, programme, analyse, favour, behaviour, specialise, kilometre, defence, licence (when used as a verb); one instance is enough to fail. Synthesis section absent entirely is an automatic fail.
score_1_criteria: All of: (a) deck contains no explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation and no thesis-pillar / 'attractive opportunity' / 'compelling fit' / 'strong platform fit' / equivalent thesis-style framing (per standards Section 9: 'No "invest" / "pass" / "continue diligence" verdict in any preliminary deliverable - pure assessment'); (b) every dollar figure on the deck appears in USD; NZD (or other local-currency) figures permitted only when paired with their USD equivalent on the same slide, and the conversion uses the FX rate from halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx that matches the time period of the underlying figure - historical figures use the FY-aligned historical rate from the FX_Rates_Historical tab for the year of the figure (e.g., an FY2025 NZD figure converts at 0.585 USD/NZD; an FY2024 figure at 0.602), multi-year forward / DCF figures apply the forecast rate by year from the FX_Rates_Forecast tab (e.g., FY2026 0.595, FY2027 0.61, FY2028 0.62, FY2029 0.625, FY2030 0.625, FY2031 0.625 USD/NZD); the applied rate(s) and the source workbook are documented (footnote, slide footer, or speaker note); for deliverables with no financial figures (b) is satisfied by default. Anchored verbatim in the Notes tab: 'All Halberd deal-team financial outputs (memos, models, decks, briefings) are presented in USD' and 'For multi-year DCF / cash-flow models, apply the forecast rate by year (FX_Rates_Forecast) - do not use a flat spot rate across multiple years.' And FX_Rates_Forecast tab: 'Apply forecast rates by year for multi-year cash flows. Do not use a flat spot rate.' (c) dedicated key-findings synthesis with 3-5 findings (per IC pre-read § 3.3: 'Key findings synthesis - top three to five findings, each carrying a clear positive / negative direction - what we believe; what we don't yet know.'); (d) sentiment / direction parseable across the findings (explicit +/- tags, pos/neg labels, believe-vs-don't-yet-know split, or visually distinct upside-vs-downside framing); (e) separate prioritised risk register with 3-5 risks (per IC pre-read § 4: 'Top three to five prioritized risks. Risk sections list the top three to five prioritized risks. More than five dilutes the IC's read; fewer than three suggests the deal team has not pressure-tested'). Acceptable for (c), (d), and (e): a single executive-summary-style synthesis slide that fulfils all three structural requirements. (f) every word in the deliverable uses US English spelling; proper nouns and registered organisation names retain canonical spelling and do not count as fails.

specific_file_locations: Calthorpe Part 7 [00:14:48]: 'NZ industrial electricity prices have run hot. Statistics NZ / MBIE track average industrial electricity at approximately 17.8 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2024. Through 2025 large-user prices rose approximately 12% on the back of low-hydro / dry-winter wholesale spikes, and the 2026 forward curve from the four major gentailers - Meridian, Contact, Mercury, Genesis - is pointing to another 5%+ rise. So a producer with a fully-renewed five-year tariff expects approximately 18-20% cumulative electricity inflation over CY2024-26. That's a 150-220 basis point margin headwind on the colony / barn production lines if pass-through doesn't catch up.' Part 7 [00:17:18]: 'Aurora's hedging position on electricity. Their two sites are on standard large-commercial gentailer tariffs - I understand from the broker conversation they renewed the bulk of their electricity contract in calendar 2024 at then-prevailing rates ... captured the pre-2025-spike price level for approximately three years of the contract. 2. Data-quality caveats and framing; sell-side framing flagged where used, source-vintage / scope / scale caveats stated, stated-vs-revealed preference gap surfaced, internal-estimate versus audited-financials distinction drawn, confidence ranges preferred over spurious precision on contested numbers.
